notes: Shootings recorded as outside rise with temperature and shootings recorded as inside do not. This is what the account in which heat puts more people in contact outdoors predicts. It does not separate that account from a direct effect of heat on people who are outdoors, because most indoor spaces are cooled, so a direct effect also predicts a smaller rise inside. Flat inside counts are also consistent with a direct rise offset by people leaving their homes. Effects that carry over from the night before (sleep loss) or that depend on a person's medication were not tested with lags. What the result counts against is a bodily effect that follows people indoors on the same day. Inside shootings are a different mix of events (domestic, commercial). The registered interval was too narrow: statsmodels' freq_weights with HC1 understated the standard error by a factor of 1.6 to 1.7 (referee, 14 November). The interval reported here is the corrected one, with the day as the unit. This claim and its twin on the other window are one result, not two.
